To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
brain-derived factors present in a bovine brain extract stimulate BBB-GLU1 glucose transporter gene transcription and mRNA levels in cultured brain endothelium.
the brain-derived factors in BBH increase the expression of the blood brain barrier GLUT1 glucose transport gene in cultured brain capillary endothelial cells.
brain-derived trofic factors present in BB homogenate stimulate BBB-GLU1 glucose transporter gene transcription in ECL cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of genes that are important to the BBB.
understanding the molecular mechanisms involved in the regulation of BBB-GLTUT1 glucose transporter expression.
the identification and characterization of brain-derived factors that modulate BBB-GLUT 1 gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

BBH induces the expression of the GLUT1 glucose transporter in brain endothelial cells through a transcriptionally regulated mechanism, possibly involving a soluble factor(s) that is not present in C6 conditioned media.
the brain-derived factors present in BB homogenate induce BBB-GLUT gene expression in brain endothelial cells through a transcription-dependent mechanism.
BBH induces GLUT1 gene expression through a transcriptional pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain-derived factors present in BB homogenate are able to stimulate the expression of the blood brain barrier (BBB)-GLUT1 gene through a transcriptional activation mechanism.
the BBB GLUT1 glucose transporter, a major transporter in the brain, is expressed in the brain capillary endothelial cells.
brain-derived factors stimulate BBB-GLU1 expression in ECL cell through a transcriptional pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BBB glucose transporter GLUT1 is regulated in vivo by brain-derived factors that are not present in tissue culture media.
brain-derived factors can induce BBB-GLUT 1 gene expression, but it is not yet clear what these factors are.
the brain has the ability to induce expression of the glucose transporter gene in endothelium that is normally downregulated in culture.
